# Package validation

These checks target Unity 2022.3 and VRChat Avatars SDK 3.10.x. They test the standalone package without the original Gesture Manager installed.

## Static checks

Run `python -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -v` for distribution and publishing checks. The archive tests cover Unity-ignored names and their metadata, empty-folder extraction, orphan metadata rejection, source identity, and asset/license preservation. Both archives must preserve `LICENSE.md`, `LICENSING.md`, the original upstream MIT notice and Meta's notices/binary. Missing license files, truncated AGPL text, removed MIT permission and manifest declarations that omit the custom linking permission must fail before writing output. When PowerShell is installed, they also execute `Build-Package.ps1` to check shared filtering and propagation of validation failures; otherwise that entry-point check reports a skip.

Run `node .github/scripts/Validate-Package.cjs` with `--dependency-root` pointing to each installed `com.vrchat.base` and `com.vrchat.avatars` package. To also check coexistence GUID isolation against an original Gesture Manager checkout, pass `--original-root` with that checkout's path.

The validator checks assembly dependencies, asset metadata, GUID uniqueness, serialized references, resource lookups, and the native DLL hash/importer/license files. Missing historical references are reported separately when an original baseline is available; they are not counted as resolved.

Run `node .github/scripts/Validate-Localization.cjs` to compare all five language catalogs, check source-key coverage, placeholders, line breaks and rich-text tags, and reject misleading Chinese performance grades or an ambiguous HSV brightness label. English display corrections override the canonical source wording; untranslated English entries use that source directly. SDK/product names, parameter identifiers and standard technical terms can intentionally remain unchanged.

`node .github/scripts/Prune-ControllerOrphans.cjs` performs a dry run of controller graph reachability. `--apply` prunes orphan object blocks in the eight built-in controllers and their matching restore snapshots. It verifies that the retained objects are byte-for-byte unchanged and rejects missing local graph references. This cleanup was applied to the initial Pro baseline after checking that other package assets and source code did not reference the orphan subobjects.

For a read-only report of external controller references, run `node .github/scripts/Inspect-ControllerReferences.cjs --sdk-root <com.vrchat.avatars directory>`. To save a diagnostic report, create `Output~/` if needed and supply `--output Output~/ControllerReferenceReport.json`, keeping generated reports with the other ignored output.

## Unity integration checks

Use a disposable Unity avatar project with the target SDK and this package installed. Copy all `.github/scripts/UnityPro*.cs` files and `UnityProValidation.asmdef` into its `Assets/Editor` folder so the shared fixtures and VR checks are present. Do not copy these scripts into a user's working avatar project for batch testing.

Run Unity with `-batchmode -nographics -projectPath <fixture> -executeMethod UnityProChecks.Run -logFile <log>`. For actual Play Mode session checks and GPU-rendered camera images, use a second invocation with `-executeMethod UnityProPlayChecks.Run` and omit `-nographics`. These runners exit Unity themselves; do not add `-quit` to the Play runner. Rendered validation images are saved beneath the fixture's `Temp/GestureManagerProValidation/SimulationViews` folder.

The editor runner creates a temporary GUI context to check localized UI caches, resource ownership, native analyzer initialization and preservation of user names/parameter identities. It also checks game-simulation tool registration, the absence of an independent lip-sync entry, default-enabled microphone settings, explicit manager binding, radial-first initialization, shared radial/Inspector sessions, radial icons, live localized tool captions, and the absence of a language Preferences page. VR installation and configuration are available outside Play Mode in the GMP component Inspector's **Settings > VR Setup** section, without avatar initialization; there is no separate top-level VR setup command. The motion checks inject deterministic input. Play checks exercise session ownership, movement publication, stop/pause/unlink/failure cleanup and restoration. Temporary-ground checks verify the absence of rendering components and use real physics to verify immediate grounding, standing and walking parameters, jumping and landing, unsupported movement beyond the floor, reuse of existing scene ground, and cleanup after stop, pause, unlink, input/startup failure, floor loss and disposal. They also verify game simulation with microphone lip sync disabled or unavailable. When a Windows microphone is available, they start real recording, check muted monitoring, inject a PCM frame into the active native analyzer, and verify speech-state restoration and recording release on stop, pause and avatar loss; otherwise those recording checks report a skip. The graph checks initialize a valid generic avatar through the actual simulator connection path and eight default animation layers. They do not establish equivalence with client-side replacement of SDK locomotion proxies. These runners do not validate physical control input, spoken-phoneme recognition accuracy, VR hardware, client-equivalent body IK or headset comfort and visual layout.

Desktop Humanoid pose checks exercise the production PC session and animation/pose-publication callbacks. They check gaze direction against a target view for level/upward/downward look, imported head axes, animated head/torso offsets and repeated-frame stability. An actual animation graph covers fresh animation whose value equals the previous tracking output. Real SDK Pose Space behaviours exercise initial-state delivery, fixed/proportional delay, one-time viewpoint capture, repeated Enter/Exit, parent transforms, independent Head Tracking/Animation and locomotion locking, free-camera independence and cleanup. For focused iteration run `-batchmode -projectPath <fixture> -executeMethod UnityProDesktopPoseChecks.RunBatch -logFile <log>` without `-quit`; the full Play runner includes these checks too. They use injected mouse deltas and do not establish physical input, the client's exact pose-space offset formula or full client IK parity.

## VR fixtures and checks

Prepare a disposable main-package fixture with `python .github/scripts/prepare_vr_fixture.py --sdk-project <existing-sdk-project>`. It copies the installed SDK packages and relevant project settings into `Output~/VrValidationProject`, references this checkout as a local package, and installs all validation scripts. It does not copy avatar scenes or write to the source project. Rerun it after changing validation scripts; the fixture retains its existing copied SDK packages and project settings.

`UnityProChecks.Run` includes tracking/calibration geometry and expression-menu/OSC checks. The graphics-enabled `UnityProPlayChecks.Run` also runs the production VR lifecycle and local-head-visibility checks. For focused iteration, use `-batchmode -projectPath <fixture> -executeMethod UnityProVrChecks.Run -logFile <log>` with a graphics device. This focused runner enters Play Mode and runs tracking, menu/OSC, lifecycle and visibility checks; it exits Unity itself. Do not add `-quit` or `-nographics` when retaining GPU visibility coverage. Run only one Unity process against a fixture at a time.

- `UnityProTrackingChecks` checks provider-origin conversion, stable-ID role assignments, source deduplication and eleven-point limits. A real generated Humanoid validates eye/bone offsets, eye-height/arm-span scaling, recenter and locomotion mapping, inverse coordinate conversion, reachable/clamped two-bone endpoints, preserved bone lengths, chest/knee/upper-arm constraints, SDK tracking gates and bone restoration. Tracking release checks preserve fresh animation channels while releasing old IK channels, including an animated hip rotation with an unanimated IK position and a dropped hand with a remaining upper-arm tracker.
- `UnityProVrMenuOscChecks` exercises all six expression controls, navigation and transient-value cleanup, parameter updates shared with desktop controls, OSC parsing/alignment/expiry and shared UDP-listener ownership. It does not require a network sender or physical controllers.
- `UnityProVrLifecycleChecks` uses injected `IVrInputSource` frames with the real Humanoid module graph and session. It covers two-trigger calibration, the eye camera, three-point/FBT parameters, manual assignments, tracking during blocked locomotion, same-frame pause, resume, head/input-focus loss, partial startup failure, polling exceptions, graph reset and restoration of parameters, cameras and ownership. Direct PC/VR switching checks cover repeated handovers, current-root preservation with the original exit baseline, factory failures without interrupting PC, startup-failure rollback, runtime PC view settings and mouse capture, held-menu release, and single disposal of each provider.
- `UnityProVrVisibilityChecks` exercises the production SDK head-chop rules, nested local/observer renders, duplicate/unmatched callbacks and interrupted-render cleanup. Its fixture GPU images verify that the local head is clipped while body/arms remain visible and the observer retains the full avatar. They do not simulate a headset display or certify stereo rendering.

VR visibility images are retained outside Unity's temporary directory at `<fixture>/ValidationOutput~/GestureManagerProValidation/VRVisibility/local-head-clipped.png` and `observer-full-body.png`. With the default fixture this is beneath `Output~/VrValidationProject/ValidationOutput~/GestureManagerProValidation/VRVisibility/`. The existing desktop first/third-person images remain in `<fixture>/Temp/GestureManagerProValidation/SimulationViews/`. A missing graphics device explicitly skips GPU-only visibility checks; injected pose and lifecycle assertions are not a substitute for those images or hardware checks.

GMP's standard distribution checks validate the included SteamVR bindings, metadata and assembly isolation; no separate adapter archive is built. To compile the optional assembly, run `python .github/scripts/prepare_vr_fixture.py --sdk-project <existing-sdk-project> --output Output~/VrOpenVrValidationProject --openvr <original-openvr-1.2.1.tgz> --adapter`, using the original Valve archive specified in [VR-SIMULATION.md](../../VR-SIMULATION.md). Here `--adapter` installs the VR dependencies and enables the included integration; it does not install a second GMP package. Run `UnityProChecks.Run` in that fixture; it discovers the included SteamVR types and invokes `UnityProSteamVrChecks` by reflection. These checks cover OpenVR coordinate conversion, tracker roles, analog gesture weights, mixed OSC hands with a native HMD, per-controller action release, origin-change event subscriptions and physical listener cleanup, unstarted/failed/disposed input behavior and preservation of existing XR configuration. The fixture without VR dependencies must still compile and pass its PC/editor checks. No check starts a physical SteamVR scene session.

For an opt-in real installation check on Windows, prepare a new fixture without `--openvr` or `--adapter`, for example `python .github/scripts/prepare_vr_fixture.py --sdk-project <existing-sdk-project> --output Output~/VrInstallValidationProject`. Use a fresh directory whose default `LocalPackages~/com.valvesoftware.unity.openvr-1.2.1.tgz` does not exist. Run Unity with `-batchmode -projectPath <fixture> -executeMethod UnityProVrInstallChecks.Run -logFile <log>`; omit `-quit` because the runner exits Unity after completion. This check requires network access and package-registry availability. It invokes the same **Enable VR** action as the Inspector's VR setup section, starts the official Valve download, stops displaying the installer, enters Play Mode during the download and verifies that installation and configuration wait for Edit Mode. It then checks the archive hash, UPM registration, survival of compilation/domain reload, included-provider registration, absence of a separate GMP adapter package, and preservation of the scene. Explicit setup must enable **Both** input handling and disable automatic desktop XR initialization while preserving configured loader identities and unrelated platform settings. Opening the settings and ordinary Play Mode startup must leave project configuration unchanged. SDK XR comparisons allow Unity/SDK reserialization to change internal file IDs. Restart-required state is distinct from a ready provider; validate an actual Unity restart separately when changing the active input backend. The check does not start a physical headset session. The optional **Install from Local Archive...** action under **Advanced** uses the same pinned-archive validation and automatic configuration for a user-supplied Valve TGZ.

After the installation check, run `-batchmode -projectPath <fixture> -executeMethod UnityProVrInstallChecks.RemoveDependencies -logFile <log>` without `-quit` to remove the optional OpenVR/Input System packages through UPM, wait for the provider to become unavailable, and execute the main-package editor/PC regression. This deliberately changes only the disposable fixture's dependencies. Retain intermediate Unity compilation diagnostics as well as the final result; a successful final regression does not establish an entirely error-free log.

Keep hardware and client comparison results separate from these injected-input checks. Headset/controller/driver combinations, physical tracking and calibration, stereo appearance, menu comfort, sender drift and VRChat IK/animation parity require the comparison procedure in [VR-SIMULATION.md](../../VR-SIMULATION.md). Record actual results in `VALIDATION.md`; the runner documentation does not establish a passing result.

## Additional integration coverage

Clickable Contacts checks ignore the legacy switch/tag preferences and verify independent, disabled-by-default tool instances with empty filters. Real SDK receivers and parameter probes exercise tag filtering, held-contact release on disable/dispose/unlink, repeated cleanup and destroyed receivers. Unlinking reconstructs a default tool without writing Editor preferences.

The motion checks also cover reference-derived acceleration/deceleration, direction reversal, forward running with independent strafe speed, Scene Shift/Space/C/Z event ownership and one-shot actions, default jump impulse and explicit height overrides. Session checks preserve external VR/tracking/posture state and verify explicit pose ownership, callback-failure cleanup and synchronous stopping. Graph checks distinguish unchanged SDK zero-duration proxies from an explicitly authored, test-only time-varying clip; that clip is never installed as an avatar animation or proxy replacement.

Game-tool gravity checks enter through the real Game Simulation toggle with default settings, then inject motion frames into its motor. They verify automatic gravity, physical jump/landing, walking off the floor and falling, collision-disabled movement without gravity or jumping, and restoration of the avatar, parameters and temporary objects on exit. They retain the real keyboard session for ownership and cleanup but bypass OS focus and physical key sampling. Low-level adapter checks still exercise explicitly disabled gravity independently from the Game Simulation defaults.

Standing-height checks use a fixed 0.5 mm tolerance against the original root height, independent of controller skin width. They cover initial contact, sustained standing, walking, repeated sessions and jump landing on temporary and existing level ground. Motor checks include small/large capsules, clamped skin widths, nonzero support-foot offsets, unchanged model-local transforms, wall blocking and overhead jump collisions. Existing scene-ground transforms and components must remain unchanged, and stepping beyond the ground must still fall.

Observer checks create two real SceneView windows in the disposable project, and test the existing-camera fallback with every Scene view closed. They explicitly select the fixed Scene observer and cover live follow toggles without catch-up, measured horizontal/vertical displacement, immediate Game-camera following without a Scene view repaint, repeated-poll stability, manual rotation/zoom/pan, independent restoration per view, preservation of the original scene camera, projection settings and free observer cursor input. Default-session and tool checks require First Person with the Scene Camera switch disabled. Player-camera checks cover F5 feature toggling, captured wheel zoom, the independent enabled-but-zoomed-in first-person state, restoration of a positive distance, finite bounds, modified input ownership and event cleanup. Camera component checks preserve existing view enum values, leave supplied observer transforms/projection unchanged and keep the avatar visible while rendering in observer mode. These checks do not replace interactive camera/input verification.

Game observer handoff checks run the regular Scene Camera tool's real update before entering and leaving simulation. In perspective and orthographic views, and after manual navigation, the original and temporary Game cameras must have matching transforms and retain the Game output aspect ratio. The avatar root and a second world point must keep their viewport positions across entry and exit; the Scene view framing and avatar transform must remain unchanged. These checks catch camera-induced apparent movement independently from standing-height checks.

Scene Camera lifecycle checks use the real constructor, target setter, toggle, update and disposal paths. They cover repeated enable/disable and subsequent Scene navigation, independent restoration when switching targets, parent-relative pose restoration, shared ownership across two tools, rejection of temporary cameras, and recovery of a lost target within an explicitly enabled session. New tool instances ignore the legacy saved preference; the last owner's disposal and lifecycle cleanup restore the camera and reset the enabled state. The fixture restores its original preferences, shared state, camera enable flags and Scene view framing; it does not exercise physical UI clicks or actual Play transitions with domain reload disabled.

Game Simulation camera-control checks obtain the registered tool and ordinary Scene Camera instance from the same module. They verify the shared observer state through ordinary toggles, View selection, F5 and zoom, including the enabled third-person feature at zero distance. They preserve the ordinary Main Camera and its current session state independently of the unused legacy preference, and verify owner-specific bridge cleanup after exit, duplicate/late startup failures, input failure, pause and unlink. Player lens checks restore custom FOV, far clip and projection size after perspective/orthographic Scene observers while keeping the Game aspect and height-based near plane. Centering checks use actual viewport projection through turns, pitch, distance and collision shortening; renderer visibility checks remain camera-scoped. These checks invoke subscribed input events and tool methods rather than physical UI or key presses.

Third-person framing checks use descriptor world height with avatar-root X/Z. They exercise different heights, parent transforms, scale, tilt, live viewpoint updates, target changes and lateral offsets under independent yaw. Mesh geometry, oversized accessories, renderer bounds and visibility changes must leave framing unchanged. GPU rendering checks verify a descriptor-height marker at screen center while preserving first-person and observer rendering. The tests retain collision, zoom and free-camera input coverage; physical controls and the exact client camera formula remain unverified.

Close-distance camera checks use an origin fixture to avoid subtractive cancellation in Unity's native world-to-viewport projection. The viewport tolerance remains 0.001, including 0.001 m and 0.02 m booms across yaw and pitch; placement must agree within 1e-6 m. Negative checks inject rotation, lateral placement, behind-camera depth and projection-center errors. Separate positive/negative large-world fixtures check the requested orbit within world-coordinate float precision and constrain direction/roll independently at every distance. Native viewport centering remains required there at distances of 0.2 m and above. This distinguishes camera errors from projection precision without changing the production camera or relaxing the common centering predicate.

The GitHub workflow builds an archive only. It does not replace Unity integration or hardware validation.

`UnityProMmdChecks`, called by the real graph checks in the Play runner, exercises the Extra Tools MMD session on Generic and Humanoid avatars. Authored clips must produce actual transform, blendshape and Humanoid muscle/bone changes. Checks cover unassigned and genuinely empty clips, independent Gesture/FX suppression, station parameters, layer/pose restoration, looping and automatic completion, ownership conflicts, reset/unlink and pause cleanup, and Mouth tracking. Transient clips initialize Unity's binding caches before complete serialized snapshots; authored curves, events and settings are also compared independently. These tests do not execute a world's Udon program or establish native-client station parity.

Free-rotation checks separate motor/body yaw from camera yaw, exercise repeated entry and held versus newly pressed W/S, convert free-mode A/D into real turning, and verify alignment on the next allowed motor step with actual displacement and AngularY. They retain normal strafing, Scene input, tilt, collision and jump/landing checks. Camera tests require viewport centering and collision avoidance under an independent yaw, with bounded/invalid values and normal first-person/observer behavior. The Play fixture keeps the real Game Simulation keyboard subscriptions and uses a frame adapter that calls the production mapper, with capture state injected; it covers Tab/input gating and first-person, observer, zoom, pause and failure cleanup. These tests do not simulate physical key presses or establish client turn-rate equivalence.

`UnityProLocalizationChecks` covers stable persisted enum values, native-language selector order, automatic script/region selection, forward/reverse switching across all five languages, cached radial captions, structured nested formats, and preservation of user names that contain punctuation, line breaks or text equal to a translated caption. It also checks the displayed SDK friend-parameter identifier, semantic mode labels and performance terminology. Only explicitly localized strings carry translation provenance; user-provided text is never recovered by matching translated sentences.

`UnityProFontChecks` opens Model Statistics and two independent fixture windows together and checks their shared language-specific font chains, synthetic weight configuration, language switching and root attachment cleanup. It checks representative Japanese, Korean and Traditional Chinese glyph availability when those system fonts are installed. The runtime tools use the inherited IMGUI theme. The font check generates a real multi-page CJK atlas with unused null capacity, checks resource stability over 200 updates, and verifies recovery after invalidating an owned material or active atlas page. Actual scrolling/window geometry, glyph rendering and Play Mode font transitions still require graphics-enabled checks; the synchronous editor assertions do not replace those checks.

The statistics checks compare all 31 metric values and PC/Mobile grades with the installed SDK calculator, including simulator components, complete Bounds, raw constraint depth, available size values and unknown-value ratings. They check component/asset state, SDK ignore-delegate preservation, separate before-processing and processed records, the 48-record session history, avatar identity filtering, stage selection and localized UI. Injected SDK event payloads test build-state correlation and actual build-platform identification. A disposable prefab AssetBundle build checks download bytes and uncompressed size against the SDK's build-report helper, matching-platform enrichment, two-decimal MB values, SDK grades, immutable observations and session serialization. Stale reports, missing bundles and collisions at the SDK's temporary report asset path must not supply an uncompressed measurement or overwrite existing metadata. These checks do not run the SDK avatar builder, upload, or third-party processors. Play Mode observations use the first Editor update, while manual Play Mode scans remain a separate source.

Run `UnityProChecks.Run` once more without `-nographics` to exercise the non-readable help-icon regression. It discards a test texture's CPU pixels, copies it through the production helper, compares GPU-rendered color/alpha pixels, checks error logs and verifies source/render-target preservation. The headless invocation explicitly skips that GPU-only check.

The Play runner also creates an unsaved avatar in the disposable fixture and runs the real SDK preprocessing callback pipeline on entering Play Mode. A controlled test processor removes one cube: both platform histories must retain 24 triangles before processing and 12 afterwards, independently of simulator initialization. This tests callback timing, not NDMF, MA or AAO compatibility. An optional fixture-only APW reference DLL can expose the upstream `AvatarPerformanceInfo`, `PerformanceInfo` and `PerformanceRankComputer` unchanged inside `ReadOnlyStatsComparison.ApwAlgorithm`, preserving the upstream MIT notice. The runner compares all metrics and overall ratings against that calculator by reflection. Add `-apwReferenceRequired` to fail if the reference is absent; otherwise this comparison explicitly reports a skip. Do not include APW's window or preprocessing callback in the reference DLL, and do not distribute it with Pro.
